A rule reads each simple command from its first word. It does not see a command in a subshell or in a script file. Only the credsync and Secrets Manager rules accept leading assignments and one sudo or env prefix; no rule sees a command after time. The Secrets Manager rule denies the AWS CLI read in each profile, with or without an AWS row, and does not see an SDK call. The rule find / * needs text after the slash, so it allows a bare find / and find -L /. A heredoc line that starts with find / counts as a command and is denied.

The extension needs an OpenViking server with viking://~ home alias support. The endpoint and the key resolve from OPENVIKING_* variables, ~/.openviking/ovcli.conf or ~/.openviking/ov.conf; the kit writes none of them and has no field for them. Context takeover, off by default, trims history only when the server confirms Working Memory for the commit; OpenViking v0.5.0 and later do. OpenViking v0.5.2 and later answer a root key on /mcp with HTTP 403, so the openviking_* tools need a user or admin key.

The package.json of version 0.7.64 limits os to linux, cpu to x64 and arm64, and libc to glibc, and its postinstall script stops on another platform. On macOS the kit offers the computer-use-macos component instead.

The registry tarball of version 0.7.24 was read. The read covered package.json, npm/install.js, the README and the Pi setup reference of the skill. File comparisons with the tarballs of versions 0.7.27, 0.7.35 and 0.7.36 found changes only in package.json, the README files, the skill and the extension. Version 0.7.27 adds the read-only tool get_tree_page. Version 0.7.35 removes no tool and adds optional parameters. Version 0.7.36 removes no tool; its generated tool list changes only the press_key description, and it adds the reference selkies-setup.md, which the kit does not use. In both versions the only package.json change is the version. npm/install.js is unchanged, and the README of 0.7.36 still says that the binary ships no telemetry and makes no outbound Internet connections. The README states the new optional routes that the kit does not set: PIXELFLUX_CU with PIXELFLUX_CU_TOKEN (loopback only) and COMPUTER_USE_LINUX_HYPRLAND_BACKGROUND. The registry tarball of 0.7.47 matches its registry SHA-512 integrity. A file comparison with 0.7.36 found changes in package.json, npm/install.js, the npm wrapper, the README files, the skill and the extension. The generated tool list keeps the same tool names and adds or changes descriptions only. package.json adds libc glibc and the peer range >=0.84.4 for the Pi packages. npm/install.js adds a 30-second idle timeout, an atomic rename of each binary and escaped log lines; it still checks each download against its sha256 file. The extension now forwards a fixed list of environment variables to the server, and the README of 0.7.47 still says that the binary ships no telemetry and makes no outbound Internet connections. The registry tarballs of 0.7.47 and 0.7.49 match their registry SHA-512 integrity. Their file comparison changes only package.json, the README files, the generated tool catalog and the skill. The install script and extension loader are unchanged. No tool is removed; snapshot_id is a new optional argument for click, scroll, perform_action, set_value and get_tree_page. The release notes name same-device uinput scrolling and rmcp 3.9.0. The release binaries were not reviewed or run. The registry tarballs of 0.7.50 and 0.7.51 match their registry SHA-512 integrity. Against 0.7.49, package.json changes only its version. The install script, npm wrapper, extension loader and MCP client bundle are unchanged; the generated tool catalog changes only its server version. The release notes and source delta add opt-in HTTP MCP and rustix 1.1.6, and fix AT-SPI application ownership and background-action readback. Between the integrity-checked tarballs of 0.7.51 and 0.7.59, the installer, wrapper and list of default tool names stay unchanged. The extension also forwards UMBRIEL_SOCKET and COMPUTER_USE_LINUX_DEVTOOLS when set. Against 0.7.62, the verified 0.7.64 tarball keeps the installer, extension loader and tool names. The type_text tool adds paste_fallback for GNOME Wayland, off by default. No desktop tool or binary was run for this review.

The postinstall script npm/install.js downloads the release binaries of the same version from the GitHub releases of agent-sh/computer-use-linux. It checks each binary against its published sha256 file. The install therefore needs network access. Without the downloaded binary, the extension looks for COMPUTER_USE_LINUX_BIN, then for computer-use-linux on PATH. Since version 0.7.47 the extension and the npm wrapper run npm/install.js at the first tool call when the package binary is missing, for example after an install with lifecycle scripts off; the extension load downloads nothing (read in the source, not run).

The tools need a graphical Linux session with the AT-SPI accessibility bridge and an input backend that the doctor tool of the package reports ready. Since version 0.7.36 the binary lists windows through the wlr foreign toplevel protocol on wlroots compositors without a dedicated backend, and it sends press_key chords through wtype when ydotool is absent and the session bus answers that it has no RemoteDesktop portal, as on wlroots compositors such as Sway, labwc, river or cage (from the README and the release notes, not run). Since version 0.7.47 a coordinate pointer action on Wayland needs /dev/uinput or the RemoteDesktop portal: the binary refuses the action without either route. Since 0.7.48 targeted scrolling sends both movement and wheel events through the same uinput device, without ydotool; ydotool remains an untargeted-scroll route (from the README and release notes, not run). The kit installs none of them; the kit doctor reports the readiness that the doctor of the package gives. The setup tools of the package change the desktop settings of the user. Version 0.7.51 reads every AT-SPI root owned by a pid and no longer falls back to the whole desktop for an unmatched pid. Its action readback follows the acted-on application; a compositor-listed window can use a title fallback for a Flatpak proxy (source and release notes, not run).

Since 0.7.50, mcp --listen enables a plain HTTP MCP listener. The source requires a bearer token, a Host allowlist and no Origin header, and refuses shell-enabled mode. The unchanged Pi extension uses stdio and does not enable this listener. The kit sets none of its flags or token variables. Not verified: HTTP authentication, host checks or desktop access through this route. The README still states no telemetry or outbound Internet connections.

The tools observe and act on the live desktop of the user. Screenshots and accessibility trees that a tool returns go into the conversation and so to the model provider. A loaded extension does not prove that a tool works on a given desktop.

The kit offers this component on macOS only. Version 0.1.42 declares no os field, but its desktop runtime for macOS is the optional dependency @amaster.ai/pi-computer-use-cua-driver-darwin-universal 0.1.4, which limits os to darwin. Its CuaDriver.app is a universal Mach-O binary for x86_64 and arm64 with the bundle ID com.trycua.driver and LSMinimumSystemVersion 13.0 (read from the registry tarball, not run). Linux keeps the computer-use component.

Its package.json, README, config, launch code and approval code were read; the package and the runtime 0.1.4 have no install script. The registry tarball of 0.1.34 matches its registry SHA-512 integrity. A file comparison with 0.1.32 found a change only in package.json: the version and the exact dependency @amaster.ai/pi-shared 0.1.34. The runtime stays 0.1.4 with Cua Driver 0.37.0 (read from its Info.plist). The change of @amaster.ai/pi-shared from 0.1.32 to 0.1.34 was read; it adds async settings and policy readers and abort signals, and no telemetry or download. The change of @amaster.ai/pi-shared from 0.1.34 to 0.1.35 touches no JavaScript file of dist. The registry tarball of 0.1.36 matches its registry SHA-512 integrity. A file comparison with 0.1.35 found the new skill skills/computer-use/SKILL.md, declared in package.json, changed error texts for a failed driver request, more structured result fields, a reorder of the optional dependencies, the dev dependencies on Pi 1.5.0, and the version and the exact dependency @amaster.ai/pi-shared 0.1.36. The runtime stays 0.1.4. The change of @amaster.ai/pi-shared from 0.1.35 to 0.1.36 touches only package.json. The registry tarballs of 0.1.38 and @amaster.ai/pi-shared 0.1.38 match their registry SHA-512 integrity. Their changes from 0.1.36 were read. The extension adds sanitized error categories, refusal recovery hints and vision failure checks. Its config, approval code, skill and runtime pins are unchanged. The shared settings reader now rejects malformed or unreadable settings and null sections instead of using defaults. The shared package adds error classification and preserves DNS failures separately from destination-policy refusals. Runtime 0.1.4 also matches its registry SHA-512 integrity; its Info.plist still names Cua Driver 0.37.0. The integrity-checked 0.1.40 extension now routes vision requests through the model registry when available. The change uses @amaster.ai/pi-shared 0.1.40. The consent code and the exact macOS runtime pin stay unchanged. The verified 0.1.42 extension distinguishes failed preflight checks from requests with unknown outcomes and returns recovery guidance for driver refusals. The shared package moves to 0.1.42; the skill, approval settings and macOS runtime stay unchanged. Not reviewed: the bundled driver implementation, unchanged shared-package code outside the prior review, and @modelcontextprotocol/sdk, which the package now takes as the range ^1.32.2, so the top-level pin does not freeze every dependency.

The macOS Accessibility and Screen Recording grants go to the signed CuaDriver.app of the runtime package. The driver starts on the first computer_use tool call, and that call can show the macOS grant dialogs. The install and the extension load start no driver and request no grant. Not verified on a Mac: the code signature, the notarization and the grant flow.

Cua Driver sends telemetry by default: the module comment of libs/cua-driver/rust/crates/cua-driver/src/telemetry.rs at the tag cua-driver-rs-v0.37.0 of github.com/trycua/cua says that routine telemetry is enabled unless an environment override or a persisted preference turns it off. The driver README at that tag does not mention telemetry. The extension starts the driver app through LaunchServices and passes it only CUA_DRIVER_PERCEPTION_CATALOG and CUA_DRIVER_RS_HOME, so a shell variable does not reach it. No opt-out for the bundled copy is proven.

The kit writes toolProfile core, confirmAppLaunch true and confirmDangerousActions true. The core profile is not an allowlist: the model can activate the deferred tool groups, which include run_script, clipboard, kill_app and install_extension. The app-launch confirmation covers the launch of an app, not each action on an app that runs already.

Pi gets the skills of the plugin only. Its MCP server aws-devops-agent, with a bearer token from DEVOPS_AGENT_TOKEN, comes only with the Claude Code plugin; the kit sets no token.
No test in this repository loads the skills with the kit pin. Not verified in this repository: a hands-on run against AWS Emulator.
